title: No dead letter queue — poison message blocks entire partition
expected_feedback: Critical: no defined policy for a message that cannot be processed. The failure path here is unbounded retry: the offset is never committed, so a permanently unprocessable message (malformed payload, handler bug, missing referenced row) is redelivered forever and every later message in that partition is blocked behind it. Fix: decide and document the policy. The usual choice is a retry counter (headers or external store) and, after N attempts, publish to a DLQ topic — checking the publish error before committing, because committing past a message whose DLQ write failed deletes it. For a strictly ordered topic (event-sourced aggregate, ledger) the correct policy may instead be halt-and-page, since skipping a message corrupts every later event for that entity. Either is acceptable; an undefined policy is not.
violated_rule: Dead letter queue exists for poison messages
checklist_anchor: A defined, owned policy for unprocessable messages
